Subject: Private VPC data flow & privacy follow-up (AcmeHealth)

Hi John  great call earlier, thanks for taking the time. Quick recap and next steps on the items we discussed around PII, retention, and the private/VPC deployment option: 

- PII scope: you confirmed the primary workloads will include patient identifiers and limited clinical notes. Please confirm whether PHI in free text will be sent to the service or redacted client-side.
- Data residency: AcmeHealth requires US-only data residency for production workloads.
- Logging & retention: you asked for options to limit request/response logging, configurable retention windows, and the ability to route logs to your SIEM.
- Network boundaries / egress: you flagged concerns about outbound connectivity from the data plane (esp. for on-prem/air-gapped scenarios).

Attached is the questionnaire we discussed  I filled sections 14 with high-level info; please fill the remaining fields and return when you can. Also attaching a preliminary network diagram that shows the Redwood Private control plane and optional data-plane deployment patterns.

Next steps I propose: 
1) You share the completed security questionnaire (attached).
2) We schedule a short follow-up with your network & infra lead and our engineering lead (Dev) to go through egress controls and CIDR/port requirements.
3) We produce a short proposal (SOW) outlining the private deployment pattern, retention SLAs, and optional HSM/KMS integration.

Proposed times for the technical follow-up: Mon Jul 26 or Tue Jul 27, 1012 PT. What works for your team?

Attachments: [Attachment: AcmeHealth_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (PDF, 120KB)], [Attachment: redwood-private-vpc-network-diagram.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]

Subject: Re: Private VPC data flow & privacy follow-up (AcmeHealth)

Thanks Marissa  good recap. A few quick answers and asks: 

- We plan to send PHI (patient identifiers + short clinical notes). We will try to scrub anything not required but need the service to support PII handling for these fields.
- Data residency: confirmed  US-only for production. Test/dev can be multi-region but flagged separately.
- Logging: we prefer request/response logging to be optional and to support immediate deletion/short retention (30 days) for production.
- Egress: Our security team prefers no outbound internet from the data plane. If an outbound channel is required, we need allowlisting and explicit IP/CIDR ranges. For air-gapped sites we can accept an offline installer with periodic manual updates.

I've attached the partially completed questionnaire. There are a few items we couldn't fill without answers from your infra team (network ports, control-plane endpoints, and KMS/HSM integration pattern).

Can Dev or your infra lead provide the network diagram details and confirm whether Redwood Private can be run with zero outbound internet by default?

Attachment: [Attachment: AcmeHealth_Security_Questionnaire_filled.pdf (PDF, 150KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Miller <jmiller@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC data flow & privacy follow-up (AcmeHealth)

Great notes, John  looping in Dev to confirm infra specifics. High-level answers from product/ops: 

- Data residency: production-only US region is supported; we will pin the control and data plane to the requested region.
- Logging & retention: request/response logging is configurable per-deployment. We can provide a no-logging deployment for sensitive workloads (no persistent request/response logs written by default) and/or ship logs to your SIEM (TLS to a customer-managed collector). Retention windows can be set to 0/30/90/365 days on a per-environment basis.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM integrations for key wrapping. We can also provide an option to never persist unencrypted prompts to disk.
- Egress & air-gapped: Redwood Private has two modes: 
  * VPC-connected: data plane runs in your VPC (or peered VPC) and by default has no outbound internet; any outbound to our control plane is allowlisted IPs or PrivateLink.
  * Air-gapped / on-prem installer: for fully isolated installs we offer an on-prem data-plane package and an optional private control-plane appliance. In fully air-gapped installs, updates are handled via signed bundles you ingest; no external egress required.

Dev  can you confirm the port/CIDR lists, control-plane endpoints, and whether we need a one-way egress for metrics/health (expected to be optional)? I've attached an updated network diagram (draft) for your review.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-private-vpc-network-diagram.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC data flow & privacy follow-up (AcmeHealth)

Marissa / team  quick technical specifics to share with Acme: 

1) Control-plane endpoints: we expose a small set of static IPs (or PrivateLink endpoints) per-region. For a VPC-connected deployment you can use PrivateLink or allowlist these IPs.
2) Required ports: 443 outbound to control-plane endpoints (optional when using private control-plane appliance). For telemetry/metrics we default to pushing to a customer-managed collector over 443; this is optional and can be disabled.
3) CIDR ranges: we will provide the exact per-region CIDR/IP list prior to install (typical footprint: < 10 IPs for control-plane).
4) No-logging mode: the runtime can be configured to avoid persisting prompt/response pairs. For higher assurance we support on-the-fly redaction hooks (we can integrate your regex-based PII filters) so sensitive fields never enter logs.
5) KMS/HSM: we support AWS KMS and external HSM via PKCS#11 for key wrapping. Keys never leave your KMS in the customer-managed KMS mode.
6) Air-gapped install: we provide a signed, offline installer bundle. If you choose the fully air-gapped option, you will run a private control-plane appliance; no external egress required.

Action items for Acme: please confirm whether you prefer VPC-connected (with allowlisted control-plane) or fully air-gapped. If VPC, send the CIDR(s) and whether you want PrivateLink. If air-gapped, we'll prepare the offline install checklist and update schedule.

Thanks  happy to hop on the call Mon/Tue as Marissa suggested.

 Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Private VPC data flow & privacy follow-up (AcmeHealth)

Thanks all  this is helpful and addresses most of our questions. Quick notes and next steps: 

- We want production to be fully US-resident and run in a VPC-connected mode with no outbound internet enabled for the data plane. We'll provision PrivateLink if that simplifies allowlisting.
- Logging: we will request no persistent request/response logs in production; short-term retention (30 days) for audit logs only is acceptable if stored in our SIEM.
- KMS: we'll use our AWS KMS keys (customer-managed). HSM not required initially but may be a future ask.
- Air-gapped: not required for our primary production environment, but we may request an offline installer for some internal test clusters later.

Next steps: 
1) Schedule the technical follow-up with Dev and our network lead  Tue Jul 27, 10:00 PT works for us.
2) We'll share the requested CIDR ranges and PrivateLink preference this afternoon.
3) Once we align on network and retention, you can produce the SOW and we'll start procurement review.
